findings.reason: without reckon/_flight_schema.py in the write paths the node either blocks on scope or lands a feature whose declared value is silently ignored, and the done-when's temp-flight-layer case is the only place that would notice.
findings.text: §20's deliverable declares the backend search path "in the host flight layer", but the flight layer is validated by FlightConfig.model_validate (reckon/flight.py:1417) against ConfiguredBaseModel with extra="ignore" (reckon/_flight_schema.py:38-46) and BackendConfig (:348) declares no such key, so a path the node writes into a layer is discarded without error; the write paths name only reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py, reckon/_backends.py and the new test, leaving the node fenced out of the one file that makes the declaration take effect

findings.reason: the node must either add a cli branch to the in-harness sentence, a second change the deliverable's mechanism does not describe and the gate cannot confirm, or drop the absolute claim and state what a young cli pointer reads as.
findings.text: §19's deliverable states a cli pointer "is never reported as an in-harness run", but its stated mechanism only dates the pointer so _stranded_launch can fire past the bound; below the bound _stranded_launch returns False and a same-host pointer is reported through the in-harness sentence (§19's done-when case 2 asks only that such a pointer "is not" launch-failed, which both readings satisfy)
